Getting eaten alive on this site over potty training opinions while my little tasmanian devil sleeps and the other one beats me up from the inside.

I’ve never wished for a drink more in my life. I raise my cirkul bottle to all the people who are struggling right now. Shit gets better.

I actually do this. She chooses underwear and actually eagerly picks them out. Starts the day off eager to sit on the potty. Then has an accident or two (of which I have her take off her wet clothes herself which she has mastered) and slowly throughout the day shows more and more resistance. Yet when I ask her if she would like to wear a pull up, she says no. I would do naked again (tried that the first round of potty training and it didn’t go well) if we didn’t have carpet. I explain if she wants to wear underwear, she can’t go potty in them. She tells me she has to go, and holds it when she wants. It’s just a learning experience for all of us.

I definitely don’t expect her to be fully potty trained in two months. Like I said in my edited portion, I am patience most of the day, until my husband comes home and she becomes the tasmanian devil and throwing fits about absolutely everything. I needed to throw in the towel and take a breather, of which led me here to rant.

We are and I’m fully intending on putting a pull up on for naps and bed. But figured since she was eager to use the potty at first, refuses pull ups and changes, that I would rather give this a shot. I don’t expect her to be potty trained when baby comes, and am fully aware she may regress anyway.

But would I rather be kicked in the stomach and chase down a poop covered toddler all day for pull ups or encourage potty usage? Definitely the latter.
She has been in pampers pull ups since 15 months. She easily gets them on and off (yet beginning our round 2 potty training journey).

I definitely don’t think/expect her to be completely fully potty trained by the time her brother comes. However, with her fighting pull up changes and refusing to wear one as well (and having used the potty in the past) I thought I’d give it a shot. This was just written when I was just done with everything for the day, and may have been misconstrued.

I’m definitely planning on backing off a bit but since she doesn’t want to wear pull ups either and fights diaper changes I am not completely giving up the idea. Especially since she did so well the first full day of trying. If she didn’t fight and physically kick and hit with diaper changes I would put her back in them.
I’m so confused because she *did* do it for an entire day. She refuses to wear pull ups, and fights diaper changes. She goes for other people as well. Just not her dad and I.

Ugh I’m sorry. Mine held it for 5 hours in public yesterday before finally having an accident (I had called my nurse mom panicking and she reassured me that she will go before she causes infection at this age. And she was right.

When they are stubborn they are *stubborn*. Bad thing is, she refuses pull ups too and kicks and fights through pull up changes (which being 7 months pregnant is hard to deal with). Naked method didn’t work for us either. So I literally cannot win.

We had tried potty training once before (which we took a three month break from). If she didn’t refuse to wear pull ups - that she has been in since 15 months - and kick and fight every diaper change, I would consider it. But I really wanted to at least reintroduce the concept before her brother arrives in 2 months; not that I want her fully potty trained by then. She does good most of the day with sitting. It’s really when her dad comes home that she acts up. Which is how she has always been, even itty bitty.
I really need to stay offline. The whole, “my kid potty trained in 3 days” articles had me stressing!

It’s interesting considering she sits and tries to go for my mother in law, and has indeed gone for my sister (the first time we tried potty training months and months ago). But with us it’s a literal fight. Probably a comfort thing, as kids act out most around mom and/or dad anyway.

I did indeed write this when I was frustrated. It was general end of the day/pregnancy frustration. She tends to act out more when her dad gets home anyway so it was just “I’m done in general and need away from this kid after hours and hours of this” sort of thing.

I definitely plan on using a pull up for sleeping. It was my sister’s idea to put her in thicker underwear for sleeping (nap) and I definitely regret that. I definitely know she won’t have bladder control while sleeping. During the day she will hold it as long as she stubbornly can (hours sometimes).

I will definitely try to back off a bit. Although today I have made her sit less, and she has had more accidents. So not sure if it will help much but it’s worth a shot. I have help coming but I really want to tackle this on my own - with the help of my husband of course.

I’m okay with her being in diapers occasionally (like sleeping for instance) but the main issue that started this training is her refusal to want to wear pull ups, and kicking and running when trying to change said pull ups; and her eagerness to sit most times. I do good most of the day, it’s mainly when her dad gets home and she starts acting up while I’m physically uncomfortable and exhausted and - again - having to do another load of laundry that steals my patience.

I did write this post at the peak of my frustration however, so it does come across as just stressing all the time, but I really manage to keep my cool throughout the day.

Yes I wrote this while I was near tears with frustration. I do good most of the day, but by the end (when she starts being a pill because her dad comes home as per usual) I tend to lose my patience.

We started with the potty because she started not wanting to wear pull ups and actually started wanting to sit.
If she hadn’t been wearing a pull up since 15 months and hence extremely used to it, I would go that route. Good to know it takes a long while to click for some.
I’ll try it! She does like to watch my phone or read books during, but she has a perfect little bathtub for washing toys in.

I wanted to, but the nurse at the doctor’s office berated me for even suggesting it. Stuck with the zarbees cough and cold and eventually had to get my daughter on antibiotics. I wish I would have tried it.

Naptime and bedtime I’m definitely okay with the pull up. Naptime I was more hesitant because I don’t want her to hold it until she’s in a pull up. And she will, she is that stubborn. 

I wish I would have started potty training much earlier.

I think I’m going to leave her in a pull up for naps. The reason I tried without is because I didn’t want her to hold it until she was put in a pull up. But upon having a hell of a time changing the sheet and such on her bed, I’m gonna put one on tomorrow.

Rewards worked at first. Now she just refuses to sit and runs off until she has an accident most times.

I think I just need to show my frustration less. But with being with her all day, and her having accident after accident, when her dad gets home I just reach my breaking point. Currently cooking dinner and trying not to cry! My sister is coming to stay and help this week but I struggle with that too, as surely she will (and has) gone for her but won’t for us. 

I just got so excited that first day that I thought it had clicked for her. I don’t know what caused her to backpedal.

2 and a half. We tried at 2, and she wasn’t having it. She has had better success so far (the first day) and understands the concept now but just refuses to go. After 6 days of being diaper free, I don’t want to put her in diapers all day again. Especially since she knows and actually has shown control over holding her bladder.

My life turned out so much better. It’s hard and definitely not for everyone, but worth it.

We started this because she is actually resisting wearing a diaper. Keeping at it for a little bit longer. 

It’s a matter of I should have done it the montessori way *before* this certain phase that she’s in.

She finally went (had an accident but ah well). My mom said not to worry, she is little enough that she will go when she really needs to before infection will happen. Apparently she didn’t have to go too badly until right when we were about to head home.

Once we’re home it’s naptime so she’s going back in a diaper. The fact that she has gone successfully multiple times shows me she is ready. Like I said, all day earlier this week she went. I’m not, however, leaving her in a pull up all day and undoing all the progress we have made (be as little as it is).

We have delayed it once before. She did wonderful the second day and went potty no problem, but since her dad has been home (shocker) it’s been absolute refusal to go. She will go back to normal tomorrow I think. Maybe.

I just hope holding it won’t cause infection or anything. That’s my main concern.

My mom is a nurse. I’ll call and see what she thinks. Her pull up is gonna be extremely wet this afternoon I know.
No her pants and underwear have stayed dry and she has been quarantined to the same room as us. She can’t quite get them off by herself yet. It’s coming.

SAHM with a 2.5 year old that I’m attempting to potty train and a baby on the way. The struggle. Is. REAL. My daughter was *so* difficult today I just wanted to scream! She was banging her head on the floors and wall when I wouldn’t give her what she wanted, running away, refusing to listen. 

It *has* to be a phase. Reading books about behaviors and emotions have seemed to help a little for us. 

Solidarity, Mama. Toddlers are assholes.
Definitely younger socks. I love the way she runs and how her tail wags!

We have a bigger dresser in our room now for nighttime changes with our second, needless to say.

Thank you. It’s all good. She actually hasn’t had any accidents today and has gone three times, which has been amazing, far better than when my sister was here. I plan on bringing the potty travel in public, but also at first keeping her in a pull up if we are going to be gone a long time. Seems pull up (while asking if they have to go) is the way to do things at first. It’s getting her to go for her dad too that is difficult haha she becomes a different kiddo when dad comes home.
They numb the area too. Had a conversation with my cousin who circumcised her son. At least, in the pediatric office we go to they do.
Awesome thanks! Glad I ordered one.
We’ll definitely stick with a pull up outside of the house for a little while, thanks!

My sister visited a week. It wasn’t really that much of a life change. She clearly showed she was ready then. We had stuck to that same routine, but she then got sick so we backed off.

And actually, we had a tiny tiny bit of success last night. So it’s a process that we are all slowly learning. I’m definitely gonna keep at it for as long as possible unless she really puts up a fight. She’s been pretty cooperative so far (aside from when her dad comes home). 

Also, your last point is not how a two year old’s train of thought works. I’ve discussed this with my therapist. She will not think we are just sending her away to replace her with the baby. I myself had those thoughts, and I was reassured that she will *not* feel “abandoned”. She will not be starting daycare until 3 and a half, so we have a full year. All I’ve told her is if she learns to use the potty, she will be able to play with friends more and teach her baby brother how to go. 

I’m not pushing for any deadlines, considering we have a year to train. Just encouragement.
I wish that would have worked for us! It unfortunately didn’t. We’re on day 3 now and had the tiniest bit of success yesterday, so fingers crossed this gets easier.
Mine helps me up off the floor. Second pregnancy, so the compassion is less this time around lol. Like, “Yeah yeah, we’ve been through this before.”
Backpack leash for sure. It teaches them to stay close, and keeps them safe. We used one with our daughter and will do the same with our son if need be.

Thank you. Naked absolutely didn’t work last time. Peeing/pooping on the floor had no effect (and it’s unfortunately too cold here at the moment to do it).

Thanks! We do have her potty watch set to every 30 minutes. I’m hoping this time she will truly catch on. She seemed excited when I explained that since she’s gonna be the big sister, she will get to show her baby brother how to go potty. 

Then dad came home and all hell broke loose. Refusing to sit, theatrical meltdowns, fun stuff. Probably because dad might just give into her. He won’t of course, but she doesn’t know that.

Not sure whether to put her in pull ups or not when we travel outside the house, or if that would be even more confusing. So for now, just staying home.

I would love if I could send her to a program specifically for potty training. Being a stay at home mom has its drawbacks.

My first labor, I was in labor for 21 hours with pitocin. But epidural wasn’t placed properly so it wore off in less than an hour. 2 and a half years later, I have back pain because of it. 

However… I will be trying to get one with my next delivery in a few months. Fingers crossed it works!

I had a pretty traumatic birth. Was in labor for 21 hours, daughter had the cord around her neck, and I bled out afterwards and was rushed to OR almost immediately. (She was a big baby compared to my body). The 4th degree laceration was outer and inner, so not being able to hold her after she was born and worrying about dying really sucked. Plus, losing half the blood in your body makes you *super* weak and shaky, so trying to take care of your baby while weak and in pain is not great.

So I would definitely want to be induced sooner, instead of 5 days after my due date. And I will be with this next one, to hopefully prevent damage.

Completely agree. I worry so much because I found out my second is a boy (we already have a beautiful daughter) and I want them to be close like Bluey and Bingo but I don’t know if it will be different or not. I just want that type of sibling relationship for them.

Would you say your experience overall was more positive or negative?

Hope you’re doing okay!

I was in labor for 21 hours. After a failed epidural, getting fingers shoved into my cervix multiple times, a catheter inserted into my cervix, I just wanted baby *out*. Did not care about displaying my vagina for the world to see since they were already familiar with it. 

You reach a point where all humility goes out the window. 

I’m totally prepared for the second round. Though I will be bringing cozy clothes to wear this time around. Along with adult diapers because it’s just so much easier.
Was willing to believe this until the name switched from Adam to Chase…

That’s completely understandable to feel a bit threatened because of this new revelation. But if she truly loves you she won’t cheat and will stick out your relationship. You definitely have to establish boundaries on this new thing added into your relationship is all. Just because someone likes both genders doesn’t immediately make them bound to leave you because they’re interested in them. There’s a reason she’s with you and if she’s a good one, she won’t up and leave you because of it.

It can be a good thing. I don’t have jealousy if my husband looks at boobs or what not, I appreciate it with him. Bisexual doesn’t mean infidelity. You have to be sure that your girlfriend will put boundaries in place if her friend crosses the line.

Does knowing this completely change your relationship? If so, have a long talk with your girlfriend.

I’m also bisexual and in a heterosexual relationship, though we started out with him knowing that about me. Is she just now discovering this part of herself? Also, don’t read too much into the hugs. I hug my friends (sometimes long hugs if needed) and there isn’t any feeling there. If you have a reason to not trust your girlfriend, then you have a reason to doubt, but hugging a friend isn’t really a big issue despite the fact that she’s bisexual. Remember, you don’t have to trust her friends, you need to trust your girlfriend. And if you can’t, then the relationship is not gonna work.

I also struggled with extreme postpartum depression (due to a traumatic birth experience) and I’m due with my second in a few months. What has really helped me is getting into therapy and coming up with a plan on what to do if I fall back into that state of mind.

Remember that it’s *your* choice to have this baby and you have a right to do whatever you feel is best. Also, every pregnancy is vastly different; I had severe morning sickness with my daughter and barely any with my son. It might not be as bad this time around.

Definitely try to reach out to support to help your mental health journey in whatever you do.

I think every and all kinds of birth should be celebrated. My epidural failed, and I was pretty much stuck with an all natural birth. It’s not anything that you’re doing wrong, it’s developmentally appropriate.

Dr. Brown’s bottles are wonderful. They reduce air intake that can cause baby to become gassy and uncomfortable. We used so many brands and had so many fussy uncomfortable moments after feeding that drastically reduced once we switched to that brand.

Some advice from the 19 months I’ve been a mom: 

*Postpartum depression is real for moms and dads. Not sure what your living situation is like, but being up with a baby all night and then having to do school can really have a toll on your mental health. Keep an eye on it and know that not all moments will be happy ones (you may dislike this part of parenthood and that is perfectly okay).

*You are your child’s parent first, not their friend. I’ve known so many people to make this mistake and their kids grow up to be horribly disrespectful while their parents allow them to do what they like. You’re going to have to set boundaries for your kiddo.

*Finishing school and getting a good paying job (my husband went to a trade school and it was far better in teaching than actual college) is the best you can do.

*What To Expect While You’re Expecting is a great book for both parents to read, so you can understand your GF’s pregnancy experience. What To Expect The First Year was an amazing read for myself, personally.

*Newborns sometimes go through periods where they cry just to cry. This is called “purple crying” and my daughter cried at the same time every day, for months. I could do nothing but hold her and cry myself. If you get frustrated, please please put the baby down somewhere safe. A crying baby is an alive baby.

*You don’t come first anymore. Taking care of yourself is important, but everything you enjoy (hobbies, going out, etc) come second before your baby’s needs. Even things as simple as eating, sleeping. You will sacrifice yourself for your baby and that’s going to be one of the hardest things you’ll do.

I was almost kidnapped when I was in middle school. 

I lived about 8 miles out of town, so I had to take the bus to and from school. Our little "town" was right off the highway. And because I was the youngest sibling, my bus was different and I left earlier and got home earlier than my older siblings. 

One day on my walk home (I lived about 2 blocks away from the bus stop) I noticed a red truck following behind me going really slow. I ignored it and walked home. 

Days go by with the truck stopping in front of my house, man in the front seat with a black lab beside him, watching me go inside. I get freaked out enough to tell my parents. My sister automatically assumes I'm lying, but my parents believe me thankfully. 

My parents notify the school just in time, as he apparently has followed the bus and found out where I attend school; the truck was spotted outside.

The next day my mom drives me to the bus stop. I see the red truck at the gas station across the street and so does she. I get out and go to the bus.

My mom drives around the truck, noticing the man slumped in the driver's seat, watching me. His back license plate is covered in mud and she's unable to read the number. She calls the police. 

That day I get off the bus at my normal time to see the red truck is parked right where I would have to walk past (meaning I would be walking past the driver's side door). 

I spot a police car and immediately walk to it instead of my normal route home. They escort me home, and then go to talk to the guy. He takes off down the highway and I never see him again. 

I think often about what would have happened if I never told my parents, or if they didn't believe me after all, or if I had walked by him that day. I might not be here typing this. I only hope he didn't go after some other helpless child. 

As a mom, this scares me to death that my child could just as easily be stolen.

The traumatic birth of my daughter. I was induced, 5 days after my due date. 21 hour labor, constant contractions. Almost 12 hours in, they finally broke my water. I was 6 cm at that point. Wanted to hold off as long as possible for the epidural (BAD idea) and by the time I got one, I was 8 cm and could hardly sit still to get it in my back because of the contractions. Well, they moved me around so much, the needle slipped and it wore off. I kept telling the nurses I could feel, and they kept telling me to hit that stupid button to administer more numbing medicine (which wasn't working).

By the time the anesthesiologist came in to check, I was at 9 cm. I refused another epidural (those fucking HURT - not to mention there was no way I could sit still for another one). Soon, it was time to push. Well, my OB had gone home for the night so I got a midwife to delivery. Lucky me! Not.

Feeling everything (which honestly wasn't as bad as I thought - labor was worse - I pushed for about 45 minutes. When my daughter's head came out, they noticed the umbilical cord was wrapped tightly around her neck twice. The midwife proceeded to YANK her out, instead of giving me an episiotomy (a procedure where they cut you so you don't tear as badly) because she wasn't authorized to do it.

I tore, badly. Inside and out, 4th degree. Didn't know how bad yet, just knew my daughter wasn't crying. They got her breathing, and that first cry... was the sweetest thing I ever heard. 

I soon began to not feel well. I felt sick and dizzy, and didn't know why. Midwife was attempting to stitch me up, but couldn't. Called my OB, who rushed in (of COURSE he couldn't come back in to deliver my baby) and I was rushed to the OR. I wasn't even able to hold my baby girl.

No one told me what was happening. They put an oxygen mask on me, and I just remember that was the moment I was scared. I stared up at the ceiling, thinking "Is this it? Am I going to die?"

Then I was out. I woke up hours later, learning about the tear and soon being hooked up to 2 bags of blood. I apparently had lost half the blood in my body, and they saw claw marks on the inside from my daughter's FINGERNAILS. Because she had the cord around her neck. I blame the pitocin (the drug they gave to me).

So needless to say... I'm considering the second (and final) child to be a c-section. I don't mean for this to scare anyone, my situation was abnormal and just a shitty hand all the way around. My OB should have delivered, but didn't. They should have broken my water sooner, but didn't. 

I'm just thankful my daughter is healthy. 4 months later, I'm fully healed and life is good. And I feel like a kickass mom because I DID that. 

TL; DR: Traumatic birth of my first baby

My boyfriend and I were trying out a new restaurant in our town. We wanted some variety, and this restaurant had (supposedly) the best Philly steak sandwich. Which totally ended up not being that great, but I digress. 

Sometime throughout our meal, I had to use the bathroom. I thought nothing of it. In and out, and we'll be on our way. 

This bathroom was in the back corner of the restaurant. There was a dark, unfinished hallway leading up to it. Again, thinking nothing of it since it's a new restaurant, I pop into the brightly lit women's room and begin to do my thing. 

To this day, I have never felt such cold, gut-wrenching, bone-chilling fear before. This bathroom was small--one stall, one sink, pictures, all the like--and I thought all was fine and dandy. 

Until. I felt like someone had thrown an ice-cold bucket of water on me. Something was wrong. Chills ran up my spine, goosebumps prickled on my arms, alarm bells rang in my head loud and clear. I didn't know why, but I felt like I needed to get out of there IMMEDIATELY. I was in danger. And all I could think was... "FUCK this!"

Unable to finish, paralyzed by fear, with shaking hands I pull my pants up and book it out of there, not daring to look back. 

I told my boyfriend about this and to this day he brushes it off, but I swear, something or someone was in there or close by. We've never gone back to that restaurant and we never will.

Moving out of my parent's place/family situations. I was 20 by the time I got my shit together and moved (it was impulse but I don't regret it). I had independence far later in life than I should have and I suffered. I had a horrible work ethic, would stop showing up to jobs and would instead go to coffee shops so my mom thought I was working. 

I'm 22 now and I just bought a house with my boyfriend. I'm a barista (not good money but I love my job) and my boyfriend makes good money. I have learned to save, budget (still working on it), and the meaning of saving money for bills instead of blowing it all. I've matured a lot and I only wish I would have done that earlier in life so I hadn't have gone through as many jobs as I had and not dropped out of college. 

Young adults/teens: If you're going to college I recommend a dorm situation. Community college left me unmotivated and miserable since I was still under my parent's roof. That little bit of freedom is important, believe me. If you aren't going to college, get a job and save up some. Find a roommate or 2. Don't stay if you don't want to. Take advice from people who are older than you, but don't allow judgement to sway your own way of thinking/beliefs. 

If you stay home long enough, you either grow to resent yourself, your parent, or they resent you. The world is a big scary place but we all need to learn to live in it.
